confirmed.title: iOS runDueTasksAsync fires/counts pure-background tasks that Web & Kotlin exclude (fired-count divergence)
confirmed.claim: The Swift backend method runDueTasksAsync delegates to runDueBackgroundTasks(), whose due-set uses isDue = `due || isBackground`. A pure background-trigger task (nextRunAt == nil) therefore PASSES, gets sorted with `(nextRunAt as? Int) ?? 0` -> 0, is dispatched and counted. Web and Kotlin runDueTasksAsync both filter `nextRunAt != null && nextRunAt <= now`, EXCLUDING nil-nextRunAt background tasks. So for an app with a background-trigger task, the shared integration entry (expo-background-task -> Conductor.runDueTasks() -> backend runDueTasksAsync, contract: 'number of tasks fired') returns a different count on iOS and runs a task the other two platforms do not.
confirmed.evidence: Swift line 99: `self?.runDueBackgroundTasks() ?? 0`; isDue line 180-184: `let due = (task["nextRunAt"] as? Int).map { $0 <= now } ?? false ... return due || isBackground`. Web WebSchedulerEngine.ts:161 `.filter((t) => t.nextRunAt != null && t.nextRunAt <= now)`. Kotlin ExpoConductorModule.kt:84 `.filter { !it.isNull("nextRunAt") && it.optLong("nextRunAt") <= now }`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Split the two callers: keep the BGTask launch handler (ConductorAppDelegate.swift:20) calling a wake-path that uses `isDue` (background tasks SHOULD run on an OS wake), but make the `AsyncFunction("runDueTasksAsync")` entry use a due-set filtered by `nextRunAt != null && nextRunAt <= now` (excluding pure-background nil-nextRunAt), keeping the same priority/nextRunAt/idOrderedBefore sort. That makes the documented runDueTasksAsync fired-count match Web/Kotlin while preserving correct BGTask-wake semantics.

confirmed.title: Swift dispatch paused-gate has no Kotlin counterpart: an FCM push while paused fires on Android but is skipped on iOS
confirmed.claim: The new Swift dispatch() short-circuits when paused inside the `!manual` block (emits onTaskSkipped/PAUSED, returns false), so a push routed through ConductorAppDelegate -> module.dispatch(manual:false) is skipped while paused. Kotlin dispatch() has NO paused check. Android's FCM push path (ConductorMessagingService.handleRemoteData -> module.dispatch(manual=false)) and the live alarm path (ConductorAlarmReceiver -> module.dispatch) reach dispatch with no pause guard. A remote push is NOT cancelled by Android pauseAsync (which only `unschedule`s local alarms/work), so a push arriving while paused FIRES on Android but is SKIPPED on iOS. iOS matches Web's 'nothing fires while paused'; Android is the gap.
confirmed.evidence: Swift 296-300: `if paused { emit("onTaskSkipped", ["taskId": id, "reason": "PAUSED"]); return false }`. Kotlin dispatch 214-221 begins `if (!manual) { ... val nextRunAt = ...; if (nextRunAt != null && System.currentTimeMillis() < nextRunAt) return false; val decision = PolicyEngine.evaluate(...)` — no `if (paused)`. ConductorMessagingService.kt:47 `module.dispatch(task, manual = false, data = data)` (no pause guard).
confirmed.suggested_fix: Add the same paused short-circuit to Kotlin dispatch() at the top of the `if (!manual)` block, mirroring Swift: `if (paused) { emitSkipped(id, "PAUSED"); return false }`. Placing it inside `!manual` keeps manual run-now firing while paused on both platforms, and uniformly covers FCM push + any in-flight alarm.

confirmed.title: reschedule/headless re-arm with BOTH a recurrence and a future one-shot loses the one-shot occurrence (native-vs-Web divergence; comment claims false parity)
confirmed.claim: When a recurrence is present, Swift reschedule() and Kotlin advanceRecurrence() compute the next fire from RecurrenceEngine.nextRun ONLY, ignoring still-future one-shot triggers. Web reschedule() does `computeNextRunAt(futureTriggers(task.triggers, now), task.recurrence, now)` = Math.min(next recurrence, surviving future one-shots). Concrete input: a task with a daily recurrence whose next instance is 11:00 plus a one-shot alarm at 10:30, fired at 10:00 -> Web reschedules nextRunAt to 10:30 (the alarm fires), both natives reschedule to 11:00 and the 10:30 occurrence is lost forever (every reschedule recomputes recurrence-only). The new Swift comment asserts 'Mirrors WebSchedulerEngine.reschedule/futureTriggers', which is provably false for this case. The one-shot-only else branch (computeNextRunAt futureOnly:true) IS correct and matches Web — only the recurrence-present branch diverges. Same root cause in both dispatchHeadless re-arms (recurrence-only).
confirmed.evidence: Swift 352-355: `let recurrence = TaskMapper.parseRecurrence(task); let next = recurrence != nil ? RecurrenceEngine.nextRun(recurrence!, now) : TaskMapper.computeNextRunAt(task, nil, now, futureOnly: true)`. Kotlin advanceRecurrence 305-306: `val recurrence = TaskMapper.recurrence(task) ?: return; val next = RecurrenceEngine.nextRun(recurrence, ...)`. Web WebSchedulerEngine.ts:377 `const next = computeNextRunAt(futureTriggers(task.triggers, now), task.recurrence, now);`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In the recurrence-present branch, also consider future one-shot triggers and take the minimum, mirroring Web. e.g. Swift: `let next = TaskMapper.computeNextRunAt(task, recurrence, now, futureOnly: true)` (computeNextRunAt already folds the recurrence param plus future-only one-shots via Math.min); drop the recurrence!=nil special-case. Apply the same to Kotlin advanceRecurrence (use computeNextRunAt(task, recurrence, now, futureOnly=true)) and to both dispatchHeadless re-arms. If the divergence is intentionally accepted for now, at minimum correct the comment's false 'Mirrors WebSchedulerEngine.reschedule/futureTriggers' claim.

confirmed.title: iOS forged-push fix is bypassable: `conductorLocal` userInfo marker is attacker-forgeable from a remote APNs alert push, so willPresent/didReceive still reach the bare-id dispatch
confirmed.claim: The fix gates the displayed-notification path (willPresent / didReceive / handle) on `userInfo["conductorLocal"] as? Bool == true`, intending that only app-scheduled LOCAL notifications can dispatch a task by bare id. But `conductorLocal` lives in the same attacker-controlled JSON namespace as `conductorTask` and is NOT a secret, so a forged REMOTE alert push can set it and still dispatch arbitrary tasks by id. #12/#14 is NOT actually closed.
confirmed.evidence: NotificationDelegate.swift:63 `if (userInfo["conductorLocal"] as? Bool) == true {` (willPresent) and :81 same in didReceive, plus the defense-in-depth guard at :99-101 `guard (userInfo["conductorLocal"] as? Bool) == true, let id = userInfo["conductorTask"] as? String, let task = TaskStore().get(id) else { return }`. The marker is created at Schedulers.swift:19 `content.userInfo = ["conductorTask": id, "conductorLocal": true]` with the comment (:15-18) claiming a sender "can set [conductorTask], but not this marker". That premise is false: (a) APNs delivers every custom top-level key outside `aps` into `userInfo`, and a JSON `true` deserializes to a CFBoolean-backed NSNumber that bridges through `as? Bool` to Swift `true`; (b) the marker value is hardcoded in this shipped open-source file, so it is not secret. A foreground alert push `{"aps":{"alert":{...}},"conductorTask":"victimId","conductorLocal":true}` fires willPresent -> conductorLocal passes -> handle() does TaskStore().get("victimId") and dispatches it; tapping it fires didReceive with the same result. `grep` confirms NO trigger-class check exists anywhere in ios/ (`grep -rn 'UNPushNotificationTrigger|request.trigger' packages/expo-conductor/ios/` -> exit 1, no matches). This is the bare-id dispatch path the fix was supposed to eliminate for remote pushes.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Discriminate local vs remote by the OS-set trigger CLASS, which an attacker cannot forge, not by a userInfo key. At the willPresent/didReceive call sites (which have `notification.request.trigger`), compute `let isRemote = notification.request.trigger is UNPushNotificationTrigger` and claim the delivery only when `!isRemote` (a nil trigger = immediate local is correctly `!isRemote`). Keep the `conductorLocal` check only as additional defense-in-depth, not the sole gate. e.g. willPresent: `let isRemote = notification.request.trigger is UNPushNotificationTrigger; if !isRemote, (userInfo["conductorLocal"] as? Bool) == true { handleOnce(...); completionHandler([.banner,.list,.sound]); return }` and the same for didReceive on `response.notification.request.trigger`. (handle() has no access to the trigger, so the authoritative gate must be at the call sites; leave handle()'s conductorLocal guard as belt-and-suspenders.)

confirmed.title: Swift reschedule ignores a sooner future one-shot trigger when a recurrence is present (diverges from TS reference)
confirmed.claim: For a task that has BOTH a recurrence AND a still-future one-shot (time/notification/alarm at), the new Swift reschedule sets nextRunAt to the recurrence's next run only, ignoring a one-shot whose `at` is sooner. The verified TS reference instead takes the min of both. This is NOT a regression (the old advanceRecurrence ignored one-shots too) and Kotlin has the same shape, so it is a pre-existing cross-engine divergence, not introduced by this edit.
confirmed.evidence: Swift: `let next = recurrence != nil ? RecurrenceEngine.nextRun(recurrence!, now) : TaskMapper.computeNextRunAt(task, nil, now, futureOnly: true)` — the recurrence branch never consults future one-shots. TS reference (WebSchedulerEngine.ts:377): `const next = computeNextRunAt(futureTriggers(task.triggers, now), task.recurrence, now);` whose comment states 'a task with e.g. a recurrence AND an alarm keeps honoring both', and computeNextRunAt returns Math.min of all candidates.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Mirror TS exactly by always considering both: `let next = TaskMapper.computeNextRunAt(task, recurrence, now, futureOnly: true)` (drop the either/or). The Swift computeNextRunAt already handles the recurrence trigger plus future one-shots and returns candidates.min(), matching computeNextRunAt(futureTriggers, recurrence, now). Apply the same change to Kotlin's dispatch recurrence branch for three-way parity.

confirmed.title: Swift reschedule clears nextRunAt to null when recurrence.nextRun is nil; Kotlin advanceRecurrence leaves the stale value
confirmed.claim: When a recurrence exists but RecurrenceEngine.nextRun returns nil, the new Swift reschedule writes NSNull() to nextRunAt (clearing it, which matches the TS reference), whereas Kotlin's advanceRecurrence early-returns and leaves the old now-past nextRunAt in place. This is near-unreachable (interval/daily/weekly never yield nil; cron is rejected at normalize), so it is an edge divergence, not a live regression.
confirmed.evidence: Swift: `let next = ... RecurrenceEngine.nextRun(recurrence!, now) ...; updated["nextRunAt"] = next ?? NSNull()`. Kotlin (ExpoConductorModule.kt:305-306): `val recurrence = TaskMapper.recurrence(task) ?: return; val next = RecurrenceEngine.nextRun(recurrence, System.currentTimeMillis()) ?: return` — returns without touching nextRunAt. TS (WebSchedulerEngine.ts:377-378) computes next (possibly null) and unconditionally writes `{ ...task, nextRunAt: next }`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Align Kotlin advanceRecurrence to the TS reference: do not early-return on a null nextRun; instead write JSONObject.NULL (or fold the recurrence branch into computeNextRunAt with futureOnly=true like the one-shot branch already does) so a recurrence that yields no next run clears nextRunAt on all three engines.

must_fix.title: CRITICAL: iOS forged-push fix is bypassable — conductorLocal is attacker-forgeable; gate on trigger class instead
must_fix.fix: All three checks (willPresent:63, didReceive:81, handle:99) gate on the SAME value userInfo["conductorLocal"]==true, so the handle() 'defense in depth' is not independent — it falls with the other two. The marker is hardcoded in shipped open-source and lives in the same attacker-controlled JSON namespace as conductorTask; APNs delivers every top-level custom key into userInfo and a JSON true bridges through `as? Bool` to Swift true. A foreground/tapped remote alert push {"aps":{"alert":{...}},"conductorTask":"victimId","conductorLocal":true} therefore still reaches the bare-id dispatch. grep confirms ZERO trigger-class checks in ios/. Move the authoritative gate to the OS-set trigger class at the call sites (where notification.request.trigger / response.notification.request.trigger are available): compute `let isRemote = notification.request.trigger is UNPushNotificationTrigger` and claim the delivery only when `!isRemote` (a nil trigger = immediate local is correctly !isRemote). Keep the conductorLocal check at all three sites only as belt-and-suspenders; handle() cannot see the trigger, so it stays defense-in-depth, not the sole gate. Also correct Schedulers.swift:15-18 comment claiming a sender 'can set conductorTask, but not this marker' — that premise is false.

must_fix.title: iOS runDueTasksAsync fires/counts pure-background (nil-nextRunAt) tasks that Web & Kotlin exclude
must_fix.fix: runDueTasksAsync (line 99) delegates to runDueBackgroundTasks() whose isDue (180-184) returns `due || isBackground`, so a pure-background task with nextRunAt==nil PASSES, sorts as 0, dispatches and counts. The not-yet-due gate at dispatch line 309 does NOT neutralize this: `if let nextRunAt = task["nextRunAt"] as? Int` fails for nil-nextRunAt, so it never gates. Divergence is narrow to exactly this case (background trigger + nil nextRunAt); every non-nil case already matches Web (WebSchedulerEngine.ts:161 `nextRunAt != null && nextRunAt <= now`) and Kotlin (ExpoConductorModule.kt:84). Split the two callers: keep the BGTask launch handler (ConductorAppDelegate calling runDueBackgroundTasks) firing pure-background tasks on OS wake (correct — they SHOULD run on a wake, nothing is lost), but make the AsyncFunction("runDueTasksAsync") entry use a due-set filtered by `nextRunAt != nil && nextRunAt <= now`, keeping the same priority/nextRunAt/idOrderedBefore sort, so the documented fired-count matches Web/Kotlin.

must_fix.title: Kotlin dispatch has no paused gate — an FCM push while paused fires on Android but is skipped on iOS
must_fix.fix: Swift dispatch (298-304) short-circuits when paused inside the `!manual` block (emit onTaskSkipped/PAUSED, return false), matching Web's 'nothing fires while paused'. Kotlin dispatch (214-221) has NO paused check. pauseAsync only unschedules local alarms/WorkManager; a remote FCM push (ConductorMessagingService.handleRemoteData -> module.dispatch(manual=false)) and an in-tray alarm are not cancelled, so they FIRE on Android while paused but are SKIPPED on iOS. Add the same short-circuit at the top of Kotlin's `if (!manual)` block: `if (paused) { emitSkipped(id, "PAUSED"); return false }`. Placing it inside !manual keeps manual run-now firing while paused on both platforms.

must_fix.title: reschedule/headless recurrence-present branch ignores future one-shots (Swift+Kotlin diverge from Web; new Swift comment makes a false parity claim)
must_fix.fix: When a recurrence exists, Swift reschedule (353-355) and Kotlin advanceRecurrence (304-308) compute next from RecurrenceEngine.nextRun ONLY, ignoring still-future one-shot triggers. Web reschedule (WebSchedulerEngine.ts:377) uses computeNextRunAt(futureTriggers(task.triggers, now), task.recurrence, now) = min(next recurrence, surviving future one-shots). Concrete loss: daily recurrence next at 11:00 + one-shot alarm at 10:30, fired at 10:00 -> Web reschedules to 10:30, both natives to 11:00 and the 10:30 occurrence is lost forever. The verified fix is to drop the recurrence!=nil special-case and always call computeNextRunAt(task, recurrence, now, futureOnly: true) — confirmed (TaskMapper.swift:129-154 / Kotlin TaskMapper.kt:126) to fold the recurrence param plus future-only one-shots into candidates.min(), exactly matching Web. This single change ALSO fixes the nil-nextRun edge (Kotlin advanceRecurrence currently early-returns and leaves a stale past nextRunAt; computeNextRunAt returns null -> write JSONObject.NULL, matching Web which unconditionally writes nextRunAt:next). IMPORTANT: advanceRecurrence also re-arms the exact alarm (Kotlin 310-312 ConductorAlarmReceiver.schedule) — the patch MUST preserve that re-arm after recomputing next; do not silently drop it. Apply the same min-of-both fix to both dispatchHeadless re-arms (Swift 226-231, Kotlin 394-400), likewise preserving the alarm re-arm. Separately: the newly-added Swift comment at 346-347 ('Mirrors WebSchedulerEngine.reschedule/futureTriggers') is introduced by this diff and is provably false for the recurrence+one-shot case — correct it (or, better, fix the code so it becomes true).
